findings.text: follow-on: assert all(target == 303 for target, _ in inner_sent) is a tautology. inner_sent is populated only at line 296, by the test's own signal_step stub, with the literal 303 (inner_sent.append((303, sig))) before any assertion runs; no production code path writes it. The assertion therefore holds for every behaviour of the code under test and can never redden, so it reports a guarantee it does not provide. The target-split guard is the disjointness assertion at line 328, which does compare the code's real os.kill targets against that same 303 and does redden if the client path signals the inner pid.

follow-on: assert receipts[-1]["target_pid"] == client_pid compares the sender record against the same client_pid the test writes into worker.json at line 438 and hands to signal_pending_step_client at line 472. The record's target_pid is written by production _write_sender_record from that handed pid, so the assertion echoes its own input and stays true even if the pid named were the wrong-but-in-range target; it adds no independent protection of the signal target over line 469 (assert all(pid != inner_pid for pid, _ in sent)), which does compare against a distinct constant.
